title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Microsoft Graph APIs for agent and app inventory and details
summary: Hold: the blocking guidance omits Microsoft's qualification that blocking SharePoint and Foundry agents only affects Microsoft Copilot Chat, not every host. The briefing also extends a read-API role requirement to blocking without supporting documentation and asserts unchanged tenant behaviour despite an undocumented default.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The blocking control withdraws an agent for the whole organisation without a host-specific qualification.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.fix: Qualify the block row's note and the withdrawal guidance with 'For agents created using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry, blocking only affects availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.' Replace 'stops use of an agent' in Governance controls with 'blocks an agent in the applicable Microsoft Copilot hosts'. The qualification is at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions.

claims.claim: Blocking acts on the selected agent and should not be assumed to block its whole plugin.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.
